Hi Maya / procurement team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Medilume asked for three changes that affect the MSA + Order Form: 1) add a short pilot SOW (Exhibit B) for the on-prem inference gateway, 2) increase dedicated GPU throughput for months 2–6 (200 additional vCPU-equivalent tokens / month), and 3) stagger billing so the first 60 days are prorated and the full monthly fee starts month 3.

I attached a clean copy of the SOW with inline notes (will send a redline after legal takes a pass). High-level commercial proposal: we keep the same rate card but apply a 50% proration for month 1, 75% for month 2, then full from month 3. That gets the pilot covered while aligning implementation milestones.

Can you confirm: (a) desired effective date for the amendment (we assumed 2026-09-20), (b) if procurement needs a single consolidated PO or two (pilot + production), and (c) any internal approval windows we should hit? If you want we can provide a one-page cost table for PO.

Next steps from our side: get legal (Irene) to draft an MSA amendment and an Exhibit B redline, circulate the Order Form update, and lock in a PO timeline.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan / team —

I reviewed the SOW and the proposed MSA amendment. High-level summary of redlines and recommendations (attached redline: Medilume_SOW_v2_redline.docx):

1) MSA amendment:
- Section 3.2 (Service Levels): add explicit callout that the pilot is timeboxed and not subject to the same throughput SLA until acceptance testing completes. This reduces exposure while allowing the pilot to run.
- Liability cap: retain existing monetary cap but add an exception for gross negligence and willful misconduct; do NOT expand the cap for pilot-specific telemetry unless commercial asks.

2) Data & security:
- Add Exhibit B sub-section for "Data Residency & Telemetry" — require customer-controlled KMS for keys, specify encryption at rest/in transit, and require a SOC2 Type II audit report delivery within 10 business days of request.

3) Billing & acceptance language:
- Clarify proration math in Order Form: include example row showing month 1 = 50% fee, month 2 = 75%, month 3+ = 100%; call out effective_date and invoice_start_date separately to avoid confusion.
- Add an acceptance checklist tied to Exhibit B (acceptance gates for the gateway). Failure to meet gates moves the production ramp by one month and pauses full billing (protects both parties).

4) Implementation and change control:
- Add a short rollback/stop-gap clause in Exhibit B so that if the gateway introduces regressions to production the customer can request a temporary rollback with a documented remediation plan (limits operational risk while protecting revenue).

Next steps I recommend:
- Jordan to circulate the attached redline to Medilume procurement by EOD 9/16.
- Laura to prepare the single-PDF Order Form with explicit line-item proration examples for PO attachment.
- Karthik to confirm whether we can meet the SOC2 delivery timing and KMS integration window; if not, propose alternatives (attestation + timelines).

I will not change the liability cap amount without exec approval — if Medilume pushes for a higher cap for telemetry, we need leadership signoff.

Attached: Medilume_SOW_v2_redline.docx (redline), Quick_Rollback_Process.docx (stub).
